page: Microsoft Azure EC96ias_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by x86_64 AMD processors, it delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 672.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance operates under an isolated host model, providing dedicated physical hardware boundaries at the hypervisor layer without hardware GPU acceleration.

Storage architecture on the EC96ias_v5 relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, as the instance includes no local storage drives. The instance is Premium Storage capable, allowing high-performance remote disk attachments to handle demanding read and write operations. In addition, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default, necessitating the use of virtual network infrastructure for external routing.

The combination of 96 dedicated processing threads and 672.0 GB of system memory provides high resource density for memory-bound tasks. The absence of bundled ephemeral NVMe drives requires reliance on external storage, which decouples storage lifecycle management from compute resources and optimizes infrastructure costs. The instance is suitable for memory-intensive enterprise deployments, such as large relational database systems, in-memory data stores, enterprise resource planning platforms, and big data extract, transform, and load pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure EC96ias_v5 is an isolated memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs based on AMD architecture and 672.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, this configuration delivers single-tenant host isolation for workloads requiring strict operational boundaries. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures, but is Premium Storage capable to support intensive external disk I/O operations. There are no GPUs or default complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. By decoupling local storage and omitting hardware accelerators, the EC96ias_v5 focuses resource density entirely on high-capacity memory and multi-threaded CPU throughput. This profile is engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large relational databases, in-memory caching systems, business intelligence platforms, and large-scale data transformation pipelines requiring sustained compute capacity.
